description: A block <match> inside an engine state-child — once with </> arm closers directly in <On>, once with named </X> arm closers inside a <div> in <Busy>. Both spellings get W-ENGINE-MATCH-IN-STATE-CHILD (one each): the match renders when its state-child is on screen at page load, but is blank on every later entry until its on= value changes. The warning names the known limitation without deciding the open (A) refuse / (B) support ruling on g-nested-block-match-in-dispatched-arm-silently-drops. No state-child diagnostic fires (the </> spelling used to mis-parse as a false E-ENGINE-STATE-CHILD-MISSING). The runtime half pins only the page-load render, which is correct under either ruling.
rationale: §51.0.B a state-child body is markup rendered when the engine is in that variant; the engine has all three state-children, so no state-child diagnostic fires. §34 W-ENGINE-MATCH-IN-STATE-CHILD is a Warning fired once per block <match> in a state-child body. At page load the engine is in .On and @k is .X, so the X arm is on screen.
